title_en: Supreme People's Court's Summary of the Working Conference on Adjudicating Drug Crime Cases in Twelve Provinces and Autonomous Regions
keywords_en: smuggling; drugs; autonomous region court hearing drug crime cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Summary of the Meeting on the Trial of Drug Crime Cases in Twelve Provinces and Autonomous Regions

Fa (Xing Yi) Fa [1991] No. 38

To implement the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Narcotics Control" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision") and to severely crack down on drug criminals in accordance with the law, effectively supporting the anti-drug campaign, the Supreme People's Court held a meeting on the trial of drug crime cases from April 25 to 29, 1991, in Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province. Participants included presidents or vice-presidents, chief judges of criminal divisions of the higher people's courts of twelve provinces and autonomous regions, including Yunnan, Guangdong, and Gansu, which have handled a relatively large number of drug crime cases in recent years, some presidents of intermediate people's courts, and responsible persons from relevant divisions and offices of the Supreme People's Court.

Vice President Lin Zhun of the Supreme People's Court presided over the meeting and delivered a concluding speech at its conclusion.

The meeting conscientiously studied the "Decision," summarized and exchanged the circumstances and experiences of various courts in handling drug crime cases in recent years, analyzed the serious situation and harms of current drug crime activities, and discussed several issues and a number of cases concerning how people's courts should specifically implement the "Decision" in handling drug crime cases. At the same time, requirements were put forward for the work of trying drug crime cases at present and in the future. The participants believed that convening this meeting was timely and necessary, and they gained a great deal. The summary is as follows:

I

The meeting believed that in recent years, domestic and foreign drug criminals have taken advantage of China's opening to the outside world to massively smuggle, traffic, transport, and manufacture drugs and illegally cultivate narcotic plants, causing drug crimes, which had once been eradicated in China, to resurface and show a trend of continuous increase and spread, reaching a rather serious level in some places. The main characteristics are: drug crime cases are rising year by year, with increasing quantities of drugs; the types of drugs have evolved from crude drugs like opium to refined drugs like heroin; the penetration of international drug trafficking activities is intensifying; drug crime activities are spreading from a few border provinces and regions to the interior; drug crime gangs are increasing, and criminal methods are diversifying.

The increasingly severe drug crime activities have become a major public hazard in our society. They have caused the ugly phenomenon of drug abuse to resurface. Particularly noteworthy is the growing proportion of young people among drug users. The consequences include not only the psychological, personality, and mental distortion and perversion of users, but also the spread of diseases such as AIDS, affecting human health, corrupting social morals, and inducing other illegal and criminal activities, seriously endangering social security and order.

Resolutely combating drug crime activities is the consistent stance of the Party and the state, and also an important task for the people's courts. According to statistics, from 1983 to 1990, people's courts at all levels nationwide heard a total of 18,457 drug crime cases and sentenced 25,394 drug criminals, including 1,284 drug criminals sentenced to life imprisonment or death (including death with a two-year reprieve). Some people's courts, paying attention to combining with the actual situation of their own regions, actively carried out special struggles against drug crime activities, convened public sentencing conferences in different forms and at different scales, and loudly pronounced sentences on drug criminals, severely striking at their arrogance and achieving good social results.

To crack down more severely on drug crime activities, the 17th Session of the Standing Committee of the Seventh National People's Congress passed the "Decision on Narcotics Control" on December 28 last year. This "Decision" reflects the Party and the government's firm determination to combat drugs, expresses the will of the broad masses of the people, and provides a more powerful legal weapon for further struggle against drug crimes. People's courts at all levels should conscientiously study and resolutely implement the "Decision," deeply understand its legislative spirit and the meaning of its specific provisions, and fully recognize the serious harm of drug crimes and the importance, necessity, long-term nature, and complexity of the struggle against drug crimes. With a highly responsible attitude towards the country, the people, and the nation, they should plunge into the anti-drug struggle and do a better, more timely, and more forceful job in trying drug crime cases. It can be anticipated that with the implementation of the "Decision" and the deepening of the anti-drug struggle, the number of drug crime cases accepted by the people's courts will also increase substantially, making the already heavy trial tasks even heavier. Therefore, people's courts at all levels must effectively strengthen their leadership over this work, making the work of severely punishing drug criminals in accordance with the law a key focus of criminal trial work. Especially in those people's courts where drug crime cases are more numerous, even greater efforts must be made to grasp this work well. People's courts at all levels should adopt some specific measures. Where there is insufficient strength, timely adjustments and reinforcements should be made. If adjustments and reinforcements are difficult, they should report to the local Party committee for support and resolution. Higher people's courts should strengthen their professional guidance to lower people's courts in trying drug cases, conscientiously help solve specific difficulties and problems, and ensure the smooth progress of the trial of drug crime cases. People's courts everywhere should give full play to their judicial functions, actively participate in carrying out special anti-drug struggles and special governance, select some typical drug crime cases filed with the court, promptly hold public sentencing hearings locally, use cases to explain the law, publicize the "Decision," educate the broad masses to consciously fight against drug crimes, and form a powerful momentum to deter drug criminals.

The meeting pointed out that the "Strike Hard" campaign launched nationwide in May 1990 listed drug crime, one of the "six evils," as a key target to be severely punished and swiftly dealt with according to law. The "Decision" made by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress further stipulates stricter penalties for drug crimes. Therefore, when people's courts at all levels try drug crime cases, they must implement the policy of strict punishment while embodying the spirit of severe and swift punishment according to law. For those drug criminals who smuggle, traffic, transport, or manufacture huge amounts of drugs, the ringleaders of drug crime groups, those who use armed force to cover up drug crime activities, violently resist inspection, detention, or arrest, participate in organized international drug trafficking activities, and habitual offenders, recidivists, abettors, and other drug criminals with serious circumstances, on the basis of ascertaining the facts and evidence, they should be resolutely and promptly tried according to law and severely punished. Among them, those who have committed heinous crimes and should be sentenced to death must be resolutely sentenced to death, and there can be no soft-heartedness. It must be recognized that without resolutely adopting severe measures, it will be impossible to effectively deter drug criminals or quickly and effectively curb the momentum of the spread of drug crime activities.

While severely punishing drug criminals according to law, attention should also be paid to implementing relevant policies to divide and disintegrate drug criminals. For those who voluntarily surrender, report and render meritorious service, are juvenile offenders, or have other circumstances that warrant lighter or mitigated punishment, penalties shall be mitigated or commuted according to law.

II

On the basis of conscientiously studying the "Decision" and combining it with trial practice, the meeting studied and discussed some new issues in the specific implementation of the "Decision" and the trial of drug crime cases, reaching a consensus on the following issues:

1. The issue of the level of trial jurisdiction for drug crime cases

All drug crime cases falling under the provisions of Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the "Decision" shall, in principle, be heard at first instance by an intermediate people's court. After accepting such cases, the intermediate people's court shall decide the corresponding penalty based on the circumstances of the case.

2. The issue of new crimes stipulated in the "Decision"

The "Decision" stipulates nine new crimes. They are, in order: the crime of illegally possessing drugs; the crime of harboring drug criminals; the crime of concealing drugs; the crime of concealing property obtained from drug crimes; the crime of smuggling substances used in manufacturing narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances; the crime of illegally cultivating narcotic plants; the crime of luring, abetting, or deceiving others into ingesting or injecting drugs; the crime of forcing others to ingest or inject drugs; and the crime of illegally providing drugs.

According to Article 9 of the "Decision," anyone who allows others to ingest or inject drugs on their premises and sells drugs shall be convicted of the crime of trafficking in drugs, and no separate crime shall be listed.

3. The issue of the "threshold for punishment" in drug crime cases

The "Decision" does not stipulate a minimum quantity standard for the crimes of smuggling, trafficking, transporting, or manufacturing drugs (the so-called "threshold for punishment"). This reflects the spirit of resolute and severe punishment for drug crimes and should be well understood and implemented.

The fact that the "Decision" does not stipulate a "threshold for punishment" should be understood as meaning that regardless of the quantity involved in smuggling, trafficking, transporting, or manufacturing drugs, punishment shall be imposed according to law. Of course, this does not mean that circumstances can be disregarded and a conviction and sentence can be imposed in all cases. Article 10 of the Criminal Law stipulates: "If the circumstances are obviously minor and the harm is not serious, it shall not be considered a crime." Article 32 of the Criminal Law stipulates: "If the circumstances of the crime are minor and do not require a criminal penalty, the offender may be exempted from criminal punishment." These provisions of the General Principles of the Criminal Law are also applicable to the trial of drug cases. Drug crime cases are very complex. Among them, for those where the circumstances are obviously minor and do not constitute a crime, or where the criminal circumstances are minor and do not require a criminal penalty, a judgment shall be rendered in accordance with the above provisions of the General Principles of the Criminal Law.

4. The issue of the quantity standard for cases punishable by death

Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the National People's Congress "Decision" stipulates that in any of the following circumstances, namely: smuggling, trafficking, transporting, or manufacturing opium of one kilogram or more, heroin of fifty grams or more, or other drugs in large quantities; being the ringleader of a group that smuggles, traffics, transports, or manufactures drugs; using armed force to cover up the smuggling, trafficking, transporting, or manufacturing of drugs; violently resisting inspection, detention, or arrest under serious circumstances; or participating in organized international drug trafficking activities, the penalty shall be fixed-term imprisonment of fifteen years, life imprisonment, or death, and confiscation of property. This provision is the legal basis for the people's courts to determine the penalty for serious drug criminals.

Because the sentencing range of this provision is wide, including both fixed-term imprisonment of fifteen years and life imprisonment or death, when the people's courts sentence serious drug criminals who have reached the drug quantity standards stipulated in Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the "Decision," they should analyze each specific case, and decide the penalty based on the facts of the crime, the circumstances, and the degree of harm to society. In particular, for cases concerning whether to impose the death penalty, both the quantity of drugs and the circumstances of the crime must be considered. Among them, some drug criminals, although they have just reached the threshold of smuggling, trafficking, transporting, or manufacturing opium of one kilogram or heroin of fifty grams, may also be sentenced to death if they are recidivists, habitual offenders, or have other particularly odious circumstances; some, although they have smuggled, trafficked, transported, or manufactured opium of more than one kilogram or heroin of more than fifty grams, may not be sentenced to death if they are first-time offenders, accessories, or have other circumstances that warrant lighter or mitigated punishment.

Drug crime cases are complex, and the circumstances vary from place to place. The quantity standard for imposing the death penalty cannot be absolutely uniform. Each Higher People's Court may, based on the provisions of the "Decision," combined with the actual situation of its own region and the needs of the struggle against drug crimes, propose a death penalty quantity standard for internal reference within its region, and report it to the Supreme People's Court for the record.

5. The issue of quantity standards and sentencing ranges for drugs other than opium and heroin

Article 1 of the "Decision" stipulates: "Drugs refer to opium, heroin, morphine, cannabis, cocaine, and other narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances that are controlled by the State Council and can cause addiction." The "Decision" provides quantity standards and sentencing ranges for the punishment of opium and heroin. However, it does not clearly stipulate quantity standards and sentencing ranges for the punishment of cannabis, cocaine, and other narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances controlled by the State Council. Many colleagues hope that the Supreme People's Court can resolve this issue through judicial interpretation. This is a relatively complex issue. Some involve specialized knowledge, such as cannabis and cocaine, and must undergo rigorous scientific verification before their quantity standards for punishment can be determined. At the same time, it is necessary to go through a period of practice, analyze a number of cases, and accumulate some experience before a relatively appropriate and reasonable sentencing range can be established.

Before the Supreme People's Court officially issues a judicial interpretation, people's courts everywhere may, after collecting and analyzing cases and conducting investigation and research, put forward an opinion, first implement it on a trial basis in their own region to accumulate experience and provide materials and create conditions for judicial interpretation.

6. The issue of punishment for joint crimes

The ringleaders and principal offenders who jointly commit drug crimes must be severely punished. For the ringleaders of groups that smuggle, traffic, transport, or manufacture drugs, punishment shall be imposed based on the drug crime activities carried out by the group and the total quantity of drugs involved. For ordinary criminals who jointly commit drug crimes, punishment shall be imposed separately based on the amount of capital contributed, the quantity of drugs involved, and their status and role in the joint crime. Among them, for principal offenders, punishment shall be imposed based on the joint drug crime activities they participated in and the quantity of drugs involved. For accessories, based on the above principles and in accordance with the provisions of Article 24, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law, punishment shall be lighter or mitigated compared to the principal offender, or exempted.

7. The issue of applying supplementary punishments

The motivation that drives drug criminals to risk imprisonment or execution to engage in drug crime activities is the pursuit of illegal profits. Therefore, imposing economic penalties on drug criminals according to law is an indispensable important means for us to curb drug crimes. China's Criminal Law stipulates that drug crimes may be punished by a concurrent fine or confiscation of property. This time, the "Decision" stipulates that the crimes of smuggling, trafficking, transporting, and manufacturing drugs shall be concurrently punished by confiscation of property or a fine, changing the original optional concurrent property penalty to a mandatory requirement that when imposing the principal punishment on a drug criminal, the corresponding property penalty must also be imposed. In the past, property penalties were rarely imposed for drug crimes. According to statistics, in 1988, concurrent property penalties were imposed on only 6.5% of drug traffickers sentenced by courts nationwide, in 1989 it was 10.5%, and in 1990 only 4.2%. To prevent drug criminals from profiting economically, the provisions of the "Decision" that mandate the imposition of a fine or confiscation of property shall be strictly implemented in the future.

8. The issue of the characterization and punishment of trafficking in counterfeit drugs

Trafficking in counterfeit drugs generally falls into two situations: one is where the perpetrator intentionally passes off fake drugs as real drugs or traffics in knowing they are counterfeit drugs for profit; the other is where the perpetrator is completely unaware that the drugs are counterfeit and traffics believing them to be real drugs for profit. For the first situation, where the perpetrator intentionally passes off fake goods as drugs for sale, it is pure deception and should be characterized as the crime of fraud. For the second situation, although what the perpetrator sells are counterfeit drugs, their subjective intent is to traffic in drugs, so they should be characterized as the crime of trafficking in drugs (attempted). However, in sentencing, based on the specific circumstances of the crime, the punishment may be lighter or mitigated compared to that for a completed crime.

Regarding drug crime cases involving adulterated drugs, if the perpetrator sells diluted refined drugs, or processes drugs using crude methods resulting in impurities due to insufficient purification, regardless of how many other components are present, as long as the substance contains drugs, it can be convicted as trafficking in drugs.

9. The issue of drug identification

In recent years, drug crime cases involving counterfeit drugs or adulterated drugs have been increasing, particularly prominent in the northwestern region. This issue has also appeared in cases where the death penalty is submitted to the Supreme People's Court for review. Therefore, identifying the drugs seized in drug crime cases to determine the type and content of the drugs is a very important issue in handling drug crime cases. Under current conditions, for cases where the death penalty is proposed, qualitative and quantitative identification of the seized drugs should be carried out. For drug crime cases where other penalties are imposed, if the shape or color of the seized drugs is significantly different from the general characteristics of the originally identified type of drug, or if there is a dispute, supplementary identification or re-identification should also be conducted. In the future, it should gradually be achieved that the conclusions of drug identification, like the conclusions of criminal technical identification in other criminal cases, become an indispensable piece of evidence for determining the facts of the crime. Regarding some specific issues related to drug identification, the Supreme People's Court will jointly study with relevant central departments and make regulations.

December 17, 1991
